assertions: [O] asks clarifying questions in rounds (not one long list of more than 5)
[O] questions are multiple choice with a recommended option
[O] offers a way to add more context in the user's own words
[O] does not define 'getting more organized' silently: it is asked about or recorded as an assumption
[O] questions in the same round do not depend on each other's answers
cases.prompt: Scope a new engagement: a landscaping company owner wants help 'getting more organized' before maybe selling in two years. Make sure we're aligned before I quote it.

assertions: [O] updates the scope or contract to cover the possible family/insider buyer
[O] does not refuse further questions because two rounds already happened (asks a short new round or states assumptions)
[O] keeps the earlier scope (ops cleanup, financial records, two-year horizon)
cases.prompt: We already did two rounds of scoping questions on the landscaping engagement (owner wants to sell in two years; scope is ops cleanup plus financial records). New context: the owner's son runs field crews and may want to buy the business instead of an outside sale. Update the scope.

assertions: [O] produces a questionnaire document (not just a list of topics)
[O] has at most 15 questions in the required part (or clearly splits required vs optional)
[O] each question asks one thing (no compound questions joined by 'and' asking for two different facts)
[O] covers all three needs: goals, where money leaks, readiness for change
[O] uses plain English suitable for a business owner
[O] asks for no passwords, account numbers or ID numbers
[O] ends with an open 'anything else' question
cases.prompt: Make me a discovery intake questionnaire I can send to a new client before our first diagnostic meeting. The client owns a 20-person HVAC company on Long Island. I need to understand their goals, where money leaks, and how ready they are for change. They'll fill it in on their own.

assertions: [O] produces a questionnaire addressed to the owner
[O] does not ask her how many employees or locations there are as open questions (they may appear only as items to confirm)
[O] questions target what's needed for a listing decision (e.g. revenue, profit/SDE, add-backs, lease, reason for selling)
[O] orders questions with the most important first or says it does
[O] asks for no passwords, account numbers or ID numbers
cases.prompt: I'm deciding whether to take on listing a bakery for sale at $2.1M. The owner, Maria, has the numbers I don't. I already know they have 14 employees and two locations. What should I send her to fill in before I decide?
